# Load necessary package
library(stats)

# Study parameters
rho <- 0.30  # Population multiple correlation coefficient
p <- 3       # Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level
target_power <- 0.90  # Target power
beta <- 1 - target_power  # Type II error rate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size
calculate_power <- function(n, rho, p, alpha) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator df
  df2 <- n - p - 1  # denominator df
  
  # Avoid negative denominator df
  if (df2 <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = ρ²/(1-ρ²) × (n - p - 1)
  rho_squared <- rho^2
  lambda <- (rho_squared / (1 - rho_squared)) * (n - p - 1)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution at alpha level
  f_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > F_critical | noncentral F)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_critical, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start from p + 2 (minimum for model to be testable)
sample_sizes <- seq(p + 2, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) calculate_power(n, rho, p, alpha))

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
valid_indices <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(valid_indices) > 0) {
  min_n <- sample_sizes[min(valid_indices)]
  achieved_power <- powers[min(valid_indices)]
} else {
  min_n <- NA
  achieved_power <- NA
}

# Get power at preceding sample size for verification

  preceding_n <- min_n - 1
  preceding_power <- calculate_power(preceding_n, rho, p, alpha)
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

# Study parameters
rho <- 0.30  # Population multiple correlation coefficient
p <- 3       # Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level
target_power <- 0.90  # Target power
beta <- 1 - target_power  # Type II error rate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size
calculate_power <- function(n, rho, p, alpha) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator df
  df2 <- n - p - 1  # denominator df
  
  # Avoid negative denominator df
  if (df2 <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = ρ²/(1-ρ²) × (n - p - 1)
  rho_squared <- rho^2
  lambda <- (rho_squared / (1 - rho_squared)) * (n - p - 1)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution at alpha level
  f_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > F_critical | noncentral F)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_critical, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start from p + 2 (minimum for model to be testable)
sample_sizes <- seq(p + 2, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) calculate_power(n, rho, p, alpha))

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
valid_indices <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(valid_indices) > 0) {
  min_n <- sample_sizes[min(valid_indices)]
  achieved_power <- powers[min(valid_indices)]
} else {
  min_n <- NA
  achieved_power <- NA
}

# Get power at preceding sample size for verification

  preceding_power <- calculate_power(preceding_n, rho, p, alpha)

target_power <- 0.90  # Target power

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size
calculate_power <- function(n, rho, p, alpha) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator df
  df2 <- n - p - 1  # denominator df
  
  # Avoid negative denominator df
  if (df2 <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = ρ²/(1-ρ²) × (n - p - 1)
  rho_squared <- rho^2
  lambda <- (rho_squared / (1 - rho_squared)) * (n - p - 1)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution at alpha level
  f_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > F_critical | noncentral F)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_critical, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}
